chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"There is no harm if a man prays in the Masjid al-Shajara and says what he wishes to say and does not say the Talbiyah, then he goes out and catches game and other things, so there is no blame upon him in that."

key_terms.الصَّيْدُ: Game/Hunting, specifically wild animals hunted by a person in the state of Ihram.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm/doubt, a common juristic phrase indicating permissibility.
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الشَّجَرَةِ: Masjid al-Shajara (The Mosque of the Tree), a specific location near Mecca associated with the Prophet's farewell pilgrimage.
key_terms.يُلَبِّيَ: To recite the Talbiyah (the specific invocation 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk...'), a key ritual declaration during Hajj.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hunting while in Ihram after praying at Masjid al-Shajara?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific rulings for Masjid al-Shajara, a site near Mecca where the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) received revelation, establishing it as a place where the strict prohibition of hunting in Ihram is lifted. The Imam specifies that while the formal Talbiyah is not recited during prayer there, the pilgrim may hunt without penalty, highlighting the site's unique legal status distinct from the general Haram boundaries. This ruling underscores the scholarly distinction between the sanctity of the prayer space and the broader restrictions of the Ihram state.
